title: Sunlight Warms the Earth
seo_title: Kindergarten Sunlight Worksheets: The Sun Warms Sand, Rocks and Water
standard_text: Make observations to determine the effect of sunlight on Earth's surface.
meta_desc: Free kindergarten science worksheets on sunlight (NGSS K-PS3-1): things in the sun get warmer than things in the shade, ice melting and simple thermometers. 100 picture questions with answers.
key_sub: Things in the sun get warmer than things in the shade.
body_html:
How to think about it

The sun warms things.

  • Sun: warm.
  • Shade: cooler.
  • Sand, rocks and water get warm in the sun.
Example

A rock is in the sun. Another is in the shade. Which is warmer?

The sun warms things.

Answer: the rock in the sun

Example

Where should you put ice so it lasts?

Shade is cooler.

Answer: in the shade

Common mistakes

  • Thinking the shade is warmer than the sun.
  • Thinking the sun gives light but no warmth.
  • Thinking water does not warm up in the sun.

faq.q: What does sunlight do to Earth's surface?
faq.a: It warms it. Sand, soil, rocks and water get warmer in the sun.
Something, like a tree or an umbrella, blocks the sunlight.
Put two of the same thing in the sun and in the shade, then touch them or use a thermometer.
